subject: Post-discovery technical run-through and integration agenda
messages:

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-discovery technical run-through and integration agenda

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet during discovery last week. Thanks for the detailed notes; the internal team and I reviewed your integration goals and we think a focused technical run-through will help align on network/topology needs, auth and data flow, and a short proof-of-concept plan.

Proposed format (60 minutes):
- 10m introductions + outcome alignment
- 20m architecture walk: model variants, deployment modes we recommend (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- 15m integration specifics: auth, keys, data routing, and telemetry
- 10m Q&A + next steps (MVP plan & success criteria)

Calendar availability (Pacific time):
- Tue, Dec 2 — 9:00–10:00am or 2:00–3:00pm PT
- Wed, Dec 3 — 11:00am–12:00pm PT

If none of those work, share 2 slots that fit your team and we’ll adapt. I’m looping in Karthik (solutions) and Marissa (CS) so they can cover architecture and rollout detail.

Attached: short runbook (stub) and a one-page pre-read with the items we’d like you to prepare (network CIDR, expected QPS, and any security questionnaire items).

Best,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

A couple of asks before we meet:
- Can the runbook include a short section on data retention and log export paths? We need to verify compliance with our internal retention policy.
- Mateo may ask about private deployment options and KMS/HSM integration; can a technical owner cover that?

I can attach a brief network CIDR doc if helpful.

Ben / team —

I can take the private deployment + KMS section. Quick notes I’ll cover during the run-through and add to the runbook:
- Private deployment architectures: VPC mode (customer VPC peering) vs on-prem package (air-gapped installer). Pros/cons table and typical timeline for each.
- KMS/HSM integration: common patterns (bring-your-own KMS via customer-managed keys in cloud KMS; HSM integration for on-prem). I'll include the rotation and audit log considerations.
- Network CIDR: ask them to share the preferred CIDR and any egress firewall constraints; we typically recommend a /22 for predictable NAT and scaling but can size down for proof-of-concept.

Attached: brief slides (redwood-runbook.pdf stub) and an example KMS checklist snippet. If Ben wants the 8:30am PT dry-run on Dec 2, I can hop on.

—Karthik
